title: How the AI↔canvas layout system works

props.covers: How a scoped AI-driven canvas edit moves from operator instruction to a validated cumulative proposal: boot perception, typed id-addressed operations, tiered results, deliberate inspection, request disposal, and finalize gating.

text.insert: How the AI↔canvas layout system works

An edit starts when the operator selects canvas objects and tells the studio what should change. The harness resolves that scope, opens a draft from the current document, and gives the model a complete textual and visual starting point. The model edits the draft directly through validated, id-addressed operations. Each applied operation returns a focused account of its effect, while look returns fresh whole-board state and renders for deliberate review. The saved board is not changed until a cumulative proposal passes the run gates and the operator accepts it.
One edit, in order

The studio owns the operator-facing session. The harness owns the baseline, scope, draft, request queue, and tool runtime. The model supplies layout judgment, while look asks the canvas renderer for the same routed visual truth used by the product.

props.title: One scoped edit, from instruction to proposal
props.caption: The model edits a session draft through typed single-operation tools and uses look for whole-board judgment; finalize proposes the cumulative baseline-to-draft diff.

text.insert:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Studio as Operator / Studio
  participant Harness as Harness session
  participant Model
  participant Renderer as Canvas renderer
  Studio->>Harness: select objects, instruct, create session
  Harness->>Harness: resolve scope, copy baseline, inject page frame, sync requests
  Harness->>Renderer: renderBoardView(current draft)
  Renderer-->>Harness: full-board PNG
  Harness-->>Model: five context blocks + board image + exemplar + vocabulary sheet
  loop study, edit, and review
    Model->>Harness: typed mutator({ operation fields, view? })
    Harness->>Harness: validate one operation
    alt operation applies
      Harness->>Harness: apply, reconcile membership, diff, lint
      opt view supplied
        Harness->>Renderer: render changed board
        Renderer-->>Harness: painted-extent PNG
      end
      Harness-->>Model: APPLIED + DELTA + lint delta + scoped digest + optional render
    else legal operation has nothing to do
      Harness-->>Model: NO-OP + note only
    else state validation fails
      Harness-->>Model: ERROR + error lines only
    end
    Model->>Harness: look({ view? })
    Harness->>Renderer: render full board and optional section close-up
    Renderer-->>Harness: 1600px board + optional 1400px close-up
    Harness-->>Model: full BOARD + BOARD DIFF + LINTS + ROUTES + REQUESTS + renders
  end
  opt dispose each user request
    Model->>Harness: resolve_request(id, status, note)
    Harness-->>Model: updated REQUESTS queue
  end
  Model->>Harness: finalize(committed, message)
  Harness->>Harness: run scoped error gate, check requests, diff baseline to draft
  alt error lint or open request remains
    Harness-->>Model: blocked; run continues
  else gates pass
    Harness-->>Studio: proposal-ready(cumulative patch)
    Studio-->>Studio: operator reviews the proposed board change
  end
Reading the diagram
The operator defines the task and its starting scope.

The selection expands through selected sections to their descendants. The harness records the resulting object ids, scope frame, and boundary-connection count, then creates a draft. A frameless document receives a locked background page frame in the draft.
The model boots with current perception.

Five blocks arrive in order: editor_state, user_requests, capabilities, style_guide, and board_state. Nested XML children are indented four spaces. The capabilities block groups sections, stickies, objects, and connections; every kind has its description, operations, named functionality, and tips, while objects adds generated vocabulary and connections adds generated fields. The style guide carries one nested aesthetic topic: “Calm and uniform — uniformity is information.” It treats matched size and gap as a peer signal, sizes content first, repeats one gap per group, uses the 16px grid only for quantization, leaves air, groups through sections, reserves red for failure and green for success, and labels edges directly. board_state supplies the full digest and diagnostics. The image hook adds the current full-board render first, the house exemplar second, and the vocabulary contact sheet third; the sheet renders every type, icon glyph, and color plus connection demonstrations, including a wire ending on a section.
The model studies first, then edits through typed tools.

Thirteen typed mutators provide add, update, and remove for sections, stickies, objects, and connections, plus fit_section; each call names one operation. look is the read-only inspection tool. Section and sticky operations imply their type, while object operations cover the closed shape-and-icon type roster. The roster intentionally gives bare type names, with icon glyphs and colors enumerated one per line: the agent chooses complete finite geometry for the content and role.
The harness applies mechanics and pushes truth back.

After every operation, section membership is reconciled from geometry. Sections hold exactly the geometry they are given and close around their children only when fit_section names them; ancestors keep their slack until named too. An applied operation returns its APPLIED line, the document-derived DELTA exposing reconciled parentId and anchor, endpoint-position, or waypoint steering changes, the lint delta, and a digest scoped to the touched section, with a render only when view was supplied. A no-op returns its note, and an error returns its error lines; neither changes the draft. look returns the whole board: a fresh digest, cumulative BOARD DIFF, complete lint list, routed truth, request queue, full-board render, and a requested section close-up. Lints explain what is wrong in prose; the model chooses the fix.
The model disposes requests and finalizes.

resolve_request marks one queue entry done or declined, records a note for the operator, and returns only the updated queue. finalize with outcome committed reruns diagnostics in the edited scope, requires zero error-tier findings and no open requests, and proposes the cumulative baseline-to-draft patch. The agent fixes each warning or deliberately overrides it and names every surviving warning id in the finalize message. outcome none ends without a proposal and explains why.

props.title: The handoff is a cumulative patch

text.insert: The model works on a session draft. BOARD DIFF is rendered from the same internal baseline-to-draft operations that a successful finalize proposes, so the operator reviews the change the model has been seeing throughout the run.

There are exactly sixteen tools: section, sticky, object, and connection add/update/remove mutators; fit_section; look; resolve_request; and finalize. The system prompt has four top-level sections: purpose, board_model, state_grammar, and workflow. There is no separate rules section; required behavior lives in phase constraints. workflow organizes work into six state-driven phases: understand, survey, plan, build, finish, and finalize, with each phase carrying its objective, steps, and constraints. Build places the section skeleton first, fills one section at a time while judging a render, closes each finished region with fit_section, then adds connections, labels, and styling. Finish uses look to review touched sections and the full board, disposes requests, and resolves diagnostics.
Key facts
Perception is deliberate.

look is the model's whole-board recall affordance and the deliberate step back for composition judgment. Its board digest is an indented containment tree followed by one EDGES block; the legend declares elided defaults, and object text is never truncated. Each look returns fresh whole-board state, cumulative change, complete lints, routed truth, requests, and renders; operation results stay focused on the region they touched.
Operations are semantic at the boundary and mechanical underneath.

The model writes thirteen entity-specific operation kinds. They lower to the six object-and-connection patch kinds used by the draft applier, document differ, and studio proposal wire. Geometry snaps to the 16px grid, and parentId supplied by the model is not authoritative because containment is reconciled from placement.
The camera frames what is painted.

renderBoardView measures object rectangles, routed polylines, connection-label chips, zoom-scaled section-title chips, and icon captions, then adds padding. renderSectionView retains every painted item intersecting its camera; boundary-crossing connections remain visible to the frame edge and are clipped there rather than dropped.
Diagnostics measure legibility; the model judges composition.

Five always-on diagnostics check covered content, containment, broken edges, unreadable labels, and crowding against production geometry, and a committed finalize adds frame-slack, a polish check that would only nag while a region is still being built. Crowding is a warning-tier arrow-corridor floor: it flags sibling gaps under 80px side by side or 48px stacked, the clearance a routed wire and its chip physically need rather than a preferred distance. Error-tier findings block a committed finalize in the edited scope. Warning-tier findings do not block, but the model must fix them or name each deliberate override in the finalize message.
Code home and architecture record
The canvas-agent's document math lives under
packages/canvas-agent/src/board
: the digest, lints, document diff, and scope resolver. The model-facing prompt, context assembly, capability rosters, single aesthetic topic, and tool declarations live under
packages/canvas-agent/src/agent
. Named cameras and static rendering live under
packages/canvas/src/render
. Embedded documentation boards are frozen artifacts; the studio agent pages are the interactive surface.
